title: Rate limits
content:
# Rate limits

Requests per minute by connected account count, the per-second window on analytics, posting velocity caps, and how to handle a 429.

You get 60, 600 or 1,200 requests per minute, set by how many accounts your team has connected. The window slides, so capacity frees continuously.

## Read your remaining requests

Every response carries the limit headers (`-i` prints them). Read them rather than hard-coding the tables below; your limit may be higher.

```bash
curl -i "https://zernio.com/api/v1/accounts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```

```text
HTTP/2 200
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 599
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1798761660
Content-Type: application/json

{ "accounts": [ ... ] }
```

| Header | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | The limit with the fewest requests left on this endpoint (per minute, per second on analytics endpoints, or the [analytics read cap](#analytics-reads-have-a-team-cap)) |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp (seconds) when the next slot frees up |
| `Retry-After` | `429` responses only: seconds to wait before retrying |

## Know your request limit

One key covers any volume, even a [multi-tenant integration](/multi-tenant). [Scoped keys](/multi-tenant#scoped-api-keys) are for access control, not throughput.

| Connected accounts | Requests per minute | Requests per second (analytics) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 2 (free) | 60 | 6 |
| 3 to 2,000 | 600 | 10 |
| 2,001 and more | 1,200 | 20 |

- **Counted team-wide:** owner plus invited members.
- **Legacy AppSumo lifetime accounts:** a flat 600 requests per minute, and 10 per second on analytics.

### Per-second limits for analytics endpoints

Analytics endpoints use a 1-second window. The floor of 6 keeps a dashboard fanning out several requests per render from being throttled:

```
requests_per_second = max(6, requests_per_minute / 60)
```

The per-second window replaces the per-minute one on these endpoints. Every other endpoint uses 1 minute.

- **Post analytics:** `GET /v1/analytics`, `GET /v1/analytics/delta`, `GET /v1/analytics/best-time`, `GET /v1/analytics/content-decay`, `GET /v1/analytics/daily-metrics`, `GET /v1/analytics/format-breakdown`, `GET /v1/analytics/post-timeline`, `GET /v1/analytics/posting-frequency`, `GET /v1/analytics/dashboard`, `GET /v1/analytics/samples`, `GET /v1/analytics/tracking`, `GET /v1/analytics/tracking/{windowId}`, `GET /v1/analytics/authenticity` and `GET /v1/posts/{postId}/authenticity`.
- **Ads:** `GET /v1/ads`, `GET /v1/ads/tree`, `GET /v1/ads/timeline`, `GET /v1/ads/campaigns`, `GET /v1/ads/performance`, `GET /v1/ads/alerts`, `GET /v1/ads/{adId}/analytics` and `GET /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/analytics`.

## Posting velocity limits

Each account has publishing caps so platforms do not throttle or flag it. A post over the hourly cap is held and published automatically, not rejected.

A daily cap or an account cooldown still returns `429` with the cooldown in the message.

| Limit | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Velocity cap | 25 posts per hour per account |
| Daily caps | Instagram 100, Facebook 100, Threads 250, X 50, Pinterest 25, TikTok 15 videos and 15 photos on Business app connections, 50 for every other platform |

- **TikTok:** the 2 counts are separate, over a rolling 24 hours. A post past the cap is held until a slot frees, not rejected ([daily posting caps](/platforms/tiktok/posts#daily-posting-caps)).
- **AppSumo:** legacy accounts have lower daily caps (5, 8 or 20 posts per account per day), and the lower cap wins. An Instagram daily-limit error quoting one is the AppSumo cap.

## How it behaves

### Zernio retries platform limits 3 times

- Platforms add their own limits, some shared by every customer because Zernio is one application.
- A platform `429` or `5xx` is retried up to 3 times. A `429` whose reset is under 5 minutes away waits for it plus 1 second.
- A later reset or an exhausted quota fails immediately with the platform's message.

### Reddit's budget is shared

- Reddit limits per OAuth application, and Zernio is one: low volume on your side does not guarantee headroom.
- At `x-ratelimit-remaining` 0 the request fails without retry: `Quota resets in Ns`, from Reddit's `x-ratelimit-reset` (seconds, not a timestamp).
- Reddit's `RATELIMIT` on posting and messaging returns `429` with `Reddit rate limit reached... Retry in Ns.` when Reddit states a wait. Treat those seconds as `Retry-After`.

### Google Ads draws on one developer token

- One token, with Standard access (no daily operations cap), serves every connected Google Ads account. A `429` means Google throttled the token or your ad account.
- The `429` has `code: "rate_limited"`, `platform: "google"`, `details.quotaExhausted: true` (Google's quota, so keep calling other platforms), `details.resetsAt` and a `Retry-After` counting down to it.
- `details.quotaScope`, when Google names it: `DEVELOPER` is the shared token (nothing on your side changes it), `ACCOUNT` is your ad account.
- Not retried by Zernio; retrying before `Retry-After` cannot succeed. Cached reads served meanwhile carry `stale: true`.
- **Connecting** while throttled redirects with `error=google_ads_quota_exhausted`. The token exchange succeeded; retry the connect later.
- Zernio adds a burst limit: 15 requests per minute per Google Ads account and 120 per minute per user, answered with `details.budgetScope` `account` or `user`. Both clear within a minute.

### Meta Ads creates queue per ad account

- Meta puts a hold of several days (code 31, subcode 3858385) on ad accounts that get bursts of ad writes, and counts `validateOnly` as a write. `POST /v1/ads/create`, `POST /v1/ads/boost`, `POST /v1/ads/campaigns`, `POST /v1/ads/messaging`, `POST /v1/ads/ctwa`, `POST /v1/ads/call`, the three duplicate routes (campaign, ad set, ad) and a creative rebuilt by `PUT /v1/ads/{adId}` or `PATCH /v1/ads/{adId}/tracking-tags` therefore share one queue per ad account: one create at a time, and at most 30 in any rolling 5 minutes.
- A create that finds its ad account busy waits up to 60 seconds for its turn, then answers `429` with `code: "rate_limited"`, `details.reason: "ad_account_busy"` and `Retry-After: 15`.
- The 31st create in 5 minutes answers `429` with `details.reason: "ad_account_write_cap"` and a `Retry-After` counting down to the next free slot. `details.adAccountId` names the ad account in both.
- Other ad accounts are not affected, so to launch many ads send the creates for one ad account one after another and run different ad accounts in parallel.
- Give each ad its own `Idempotency-Key` and send the same key on every retry ([idempotency](/guides/idempotency)). Wait `Retry-After` first: a retry sent sooner waits behind the create still running, or is refused again while the 5-minute window is full.

### Upstream `429`s keep the `rate_limited` code

- When a platform or upstream service answers `429` to a direct request (not a scheduled publish), Zernio returns `429` with `code: "rate_limited"`, plus `Retry-After` whenever the upstream said how long.
- Covers platform quotas (Reddit's on inbox replies) and the billing backend behind `/v1/usage` and `/v1/billing/*`. Wait `Retry-After` seconds and retry.

### TikTok caps direct posting per application

- TikTok caps distinct accounts direct-posting through one application per rolling 24 hours, shared across Zernio's developer app. Business app accounts (every new connection) are exempt.
- Error text, priority rules and the draft workaround: [TikTok page](/platforms/tiktok/posts#direct-posting-at-capacity).

### Analytics reads have a team cap

- API-key reads of stored analytics share a cap per team, on a 30-second sliding window, on top of your per-minute or per-second limit. Dashboard requests do not count.
- Each group counts separately:

| Group (`details.scope`) | Endpoints | Requests per 30 seconds |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign-analytics` | `GET /v1/ads/campaigns/{campaignId}/analytics` | 120 |
| `ad-analytics` | `GET /v1/ads/{adId}/analytics` | 300 |
| `ads-listings` | `GET /v1/ads`, `GET /v1/ads/tree`, `GET /v1/ads/timeline`, `GET /v1/ads/campaigns`, `GET /v1/ads/performance`, `GET /v1/ads/alerts` | 150 |
| `post-analytics` | `GET /v1/analytics` and its stored-metrics routes, including `/v1/analytics/inbox/*`. Live platform routes such as `/v1/analytics/instagram/*` are not included. | 300 |

- Past a cap the API answers `429` with `Retry-After`, `details.scope` and `details.window`, and `X-RateLimit-*` describe that cap.
- To read many ads or campaigns, make one request to `GET /v1/ads/tree` instead of one request each, and run scheduled jobs with limited concurrency.

### Analytics queries in flight are capped

- Each user can have at most 50 queries to the analytics store running at the same time, across all of their API keys and dashboard sessions. It counts queries in flight, not requests per window, so requests sent one after another never reach it.
- Past the cap the API answers `429` with `code: "rate_limited"`, `Retry-After: 2` and `details.scope: "concurrent_analytics_queries"`.
- One endpoint can run several queries, so cap your own parallel analytics requests well below 50, and read many objects in one request where you can.

### Analytics responses are cached

- Post analytics are cached for 60 minutes; a stale-cache request triggers a background refresh.
- Follower stats refresh once a day. YouTube daily views arrive 2 to 3 days late from YouTube's Analytics API ([analytics endpoints](/analytics/get-analytics)).

## If it fails

A full window returns `429`:

```json
{
  "error": "Rate limit exceeded. Please retry after 12 seconds.",
  "details": { "currentCount": 601, "limit": 600, "retryAfterSeconds": 12 }
}
```

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `429` with `error` and `details` only | Your window is full. No `code`: branch on the status. | Wait `Retry-After` seconds (relative, so clock skew is harmless; `details.retryAfterSeconds` matches), then retry. |
| `429` with `type: "rate_limit_error"` and `code: "rate_limited"` | An endpoint-specific quota, such as Google Ads. | See [How it behaves](#how-it-behaves). |
| `429` on an analytics read with `details.scope` | Your team sent too many reads of that group in 30 seconds. | Wait `Retry-After` seconds, lower your concurrency, and read many objects at once ([analytics read cap](#analytics-reads-have-a-team-cap)). |
| `429` with `details.scope: "concurrent_analytics_queries"` | Too many of your analytics requests ran at the same time. | Wait `Retry-After` seconds and send fewer requests in parallel ([queries in flight](#analytics-queries-in-flight-are-capped)). |
| `429` on a Meta Ads create with `details.reason` | Creates for one ad account sent in parallel (`ad_account_busy`) or more than 30 in 5 minutes (`ad_account_write_cap`). | Send creates for that ad account one after another and wait `Retry-After` ([Meta Ads creates](#meta-ads-creates-queue-per-ad-account)). |
| Hitting the limit often | Too much polling. | Use [webhooks](/webhooks) for status, [bulk upload](/posts/bulk-upload-posts) for many posts, and `limit` and `skip` to page lists. |

## Related

- [Error handling](/guides/error-handling): the `429` envelope and `rate_limit_error`.
- [Idempotency & safe retries](/guides/idempotency): retry a create without double-posting.
- [Multi-tenant](/multi-tenant): scoped keys and per-customer queues.
- [Analytics](/analytics/get-analytics): the endpoints on the per-second window.
